title: Pilot success canvas and workshop notes - Zephyr Health
content:
Summary:
This document captures the kickoff workshop notes, technical canvas, minimal viable success criteria, and an operations checklist for the Zephyr Health pilot. The pilot aims to validate Redwood Dedicated inference for clinical summarization workloads (EHR->structured summary) over a two-week sprint with a targeted 10k inference calls/day traffic profile during testing windows.

High-level objectives:
- Validate end-to-end inference latency and cost at pilot scale (10k/day test bursts).
- Confirm output quality on clinical summarization eval set (medical precision & recall targets).
- Demonstrate secure private deployment connectivity (VPC peering + KMS).
- Surface operational runbooks for failover and scaling to dedicated capacity.

Workshop notes (2025-02-10 session):
Attendees: Ava (owner), Ethan (solutions eng), Priya (platform PM), Liam (SRE), Sofia (customer eng) + Zephyr engineers (Dr. Nguyen, Sam Torres)
Key decisions made:
- Use r-infer-3b-quant (verified by runtime) for initial baseline; fallback to r-infer-7b-q4 when latency allows.
- Tokenization and prompt template will be canonicalized by Zephyr; Redwood to host the tokenizer as part of pre-stage.
- Data for test runs: 500 de-identified EHR examples provided by Zephyr (sftp intake).
- Security: customer requests HSM-backed KMS; Redwood to provide KMS integration doc and test creds.

Sprint plan (two-week):
Week 0 (pre-work): credentials, test data ingest, simple smoke test on hosted API.
Week 1: private deployment, model loading tests, baseline latency/throughput runs.
Week 2: quality evaluation, failover tests, cost/runbook handoff, final acceptance demo.

Minimal Viable Success Criteria (quantified where possible):
- Latency: p95 inference latency <= 350ms for summary requests with 512-token context during steady state (10k/day burst).
- Throughput: sustained 250 requests/minute during 30-minute test bursts without queue growth.
- Quality: F1 score >= 0.78 on Zephyr clinical-summ eval set (500 cases) and no more than 5% clinically unsafe hallucinations as flagged by Zephyr SME review.
- Cost: per-1k-token cost estimate within 20% of preliminary projection supplied to Zephyr by finance.
- Security: successful end-to-end demonstration of KMS key wrap/unwrapping and VPC-only API access.
- Reliability: zero silent failures for 48-hour soak; observed error rate <= 0.5% for pilot traffic.

Technical Canvas (quick reference):
- Inference topology: customer VPC -> Redwood Private control plane (management) + Dedicated inference pool (GPU nodes) in same region.
- Model: r-infer-3b-quant (primary), r-infer-7b-q4 (fallback, costlier).
- Tokenization: shared tokenizer artifact v1.2.
- Prompt pattern: system + patient_history + instruction; canonical templates in linked Confluence page.
- Caching: prefix caching enabled for frequent prompt prefixes; TTL 10m for KV cache.

Test plan & sample vectors:
- Smoke: 25 short transcripts (100-200 tokens) to validate connectivity and basic outputs.
- Load: 1k request burst with randomized inter-arrival to simulate peak.
- Soak: 48-hour steady run at 2k/day to assert stability.
- Quality: full 500-case eval with SME labeling for safety flags.
- Regression: 5 known-edge prompts (previously failing) to ensure no regressions after deployment.

Operational checklist (pre-demo):
- [ ] Confirm Zephyr provided SFTP endpoint and sample files ingested.
- [ ] KMS integration tested with Zephyr test key; HSM verification planned.
- [ ] Canary deploy configured: 10% traffic -> fallback policy set at errors > 2%.
- [ ] Observability: dashboards configured (token-level cost, latency p50/p95/p99, error breakdown).
- [ ] Alerts: paging for latency p95 > 500ms, error rate > 1% sustained for 5m.
- [ ] Runbooks: rollback to hosted-api entrypoint documented and tested.

Monitoring & dashboards (references):
- Dashboard: pilot/zephyr/latency-cost (token-level breakdown, model split).
- Trace: per-request trace id will be provided in responses for correlation.
- Logs: infra logs retained 7 days by default for pilot; customer requested 30-day retention (add-on discussion).

Fallback and degradation strategy:
- Soft-fallback: route to r-infer-7b-q4 if p95 latency or OOMs observed on primary; warn app with degraded-latency header.
- Hard-fallback: abort to hosted-api (multi-tenant) if Dedicated pool depleted, with throttling to preserve capacity.
- Cache-first: enable prefix cache to reduce tokens when repeated templates appear.

Roles & responsibilities (who does what):
- Redwood Solutions (Ethan): lead deployment and acceptance test coordination.
- Redwood SRE (Liam): infra sizing, autoscaling policy, and on-call for pilot window.
- Redwood PM (Priya): track success criteria, commercial acceptance, cost verification.
- Customer (Dr. Nguyen / Sam): provide eval labels, confirm clinical acceptance, provide remediation list for hallucinations.
- Customer Eng (Sofia): day-to-day liaison and demo host.

Open questions / risks raised in workshop:
- Q1: Will the de-identified data format require extra parsing? Action: Zephyr to share 3 raw samples by 2025-02-12.
- Q2: Does Zephyr require SOC2-unique controls for pilot? Action: security to confirm minimal controls for pilot by 2025-02-13.
- Risk: Potential under-estimate of GPU memory when serving long histories (>2k tokens). Mitigation: run a memory profile on week 1 and align quantization knobs.

Acceptance demo checklist (demo day):
- [ ] Live run of 10 sample EHRs with inference and annotated SME feedback.
- [ ] Show dashboards with p95 latency and tokens/cost for the run.
- [ ] Walk through KMS handshake and confirm no plaintext keys in logs.
- [ ] Present F1 and hallucination rate from the 500-case eval.

Follow-ups (action items):
- Redwood: deliver pre-stage tokenizer container + quickstart script by 2025-02-12.
- Zephyr: upload full 500-case eval set to SFTP by 2025-02-12.
- Security: provide HSM/KMS access checklist and meeting for handshake (owner: Liam) by 2025-02-13.
- Finance: produce updated per-1k-token cost estimate including Dedicated overhead by 2025-02-14.

Notes and informal thoughts (working):
- Consider a small batching window (5-10ms) to improve throughput without materially affecting p95 for short prompts.
- Track prompt-template drift in the first week; small template changes can shift quality significantly.
- Keep the canary conservative: initial canary at 5% might be safer given clinical domain.

End of document.
